chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Muthanna from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a woman: does she perform Hajj without her wali (guardian)? He said, 'Yes, if she is a trustworthy woman who performs Hajj with her Muslim brother.'
ai.seo_question: Can a woman perform Hajj without a male guardian in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the condition of 'trustworthiness' (ma'munah) is interpreted by Shia jurists as ensuring safety from fitnah (temptation) and reliable companionship, rather than merely moral piety. This ruling highlights the pragmatic flexibility in Shia fiqh, allowing women to perform Hajj independently if accompanied by a trustworthy male relative like a brother, thereby balancing religious obligation with social security.
